eosb_termination.summary_en: Article 84. When the employer ends the contract, or a fixed-term contract expires, the employer pays an end-of-service award of half a month's wage for each of the first 5 years and one month's wage for each later year. The basis is the LAST wage. The Law's interpretive rule (Article 2) reads an unqualified 'wage' as the ACTUAL wage: basic wage plus all periodic increments and allowances, such as housing and transport. Parts of a year count pro rata. The parties may agree to exclude all or part of commissions, percentages and similar variable components from the award base.
eosb_termination.summary_ar: المادة 84: إذا انتهت علاقة العمل وجب على صاحب العمل دفع مكافأة نهاية خدمة قدرها أجر نصف شهر عن كل سنة من السنوات الخمس الأولى، وأجر شهر عن كل سنة من السنوات التالية، وتُحسب على أساس الأجر الأخير (الأجر الفعلي: الأساسي مع جميع البدلات والزيادات الدورية)، ويستحق العامل مكافأة عن أجزاء السنة بنسبة ما قضاه منها في العمل.

eosb_termination.notes: The tiers and 'last wage' basis are confirmed by MHRSD pages. The 'actual wage' reading comes from the Article 2 interpretive rule, reported by secondary sources and widely applied; some calculators wrongly use basic only. No source reports that M/44 (2025) changed Article 84, but I could not read the consolidated post-amendment text. The 'commissions may be excluded by agreement' clause was seen in an MHRSD excerpt; I did not verify its exact current article placement. Days of unpaid leave are generally excluded from service length (implementing regulations, not verified).

eosb_resignation.summary_en: Article 85. A worker who resigns from an indefinite contract gets 1/3 of the Article 84 award after at least 2 and no more than 5 years of continuous service. After more than 5 and fewer than 10 years, the share is 2/3. At 10 years or more, the worker gets the full award. Under 2 years, nothing is due.
eosb_resignation.summary_ar: المادة 85: إذا كان انتهاء علاقة العمل بسبب استقالة العامل، يستحق ثلث المكافأة إذا كانت مدة خدمته لا تقل عن سنتين ولا تزيد على خمس سنوات، وثلثيها إذا زادت على خمس سنوات ولم تبلغ عشر سنوات، والمكافأة كاملة إذا بلغت عشر سنوات فأكثر، ولا يستحق شيئاً إذا قلت عن سنتين.

eosb_resignation.notes: M/44 added a statutory definition of resignation and an Article 79 bis resignation procedure. The procedure is reported (secondary) as automatic acceptance if the employer does not respond within 30 days, with the employer able to defer up to 60 days. Neither source reports a change to the 85 fractions. Most calculators apply the fraction to the whole award; this matches the MHRSD wording.

eosb_full_award_exceptions.summary_en: Article 87 is an exception to Article 85: the worker gets the FULL award despite leaving voluntarily in two cases. The first is leaving because of force majeure beyond the worker's control. The second is a female worker ending the contract within 6 months of her marriage contract or within 3 months of giving birth. Separately, under Article 81 a worker who leaves without notice because of specified employer breaches keeps all statutory rights, including the full award. Common examples of such breaches are non-payment of wages, assault and fraud.
eosb_full_award_exceptions.summary_ar: المادة 87: يستحق العامل المكافأة كاملة إذا ترك العمل نتيجة لقوة قاهرة خارجة عن إرادته، أو إذا أنهت العاملة العقد خلال ستة أشهر من تاريخ عقد زواجها أو خلال ثلاثة أشهر من تاريخ وضعها. كما يحتفظ العامل بحقوقه النظامية كاملة إذا ترك العمل وفق حالات المادة 81.

Article 81 (full rights on justified departure) comes from secondary sources and its list of cases was not verified in this pass. Whether a resigning worker with under 2 years gets the full award under Article 87: secondary sources say yes, regardless of service length. No 2025 change was reported.

overtime.summary_en: Article 107, as amended in 2025. Overtime pay per hour = the hourly ACTUAL wage + 50% of the hourly BASIC wage. MHRSD's worked example: actual wage / 30 days / 8 hours = hourly wage. Work on weekly rest days and official holidays is treated as overtime. The 2025 amendment allows the employer, with the worker's consent, to grant paid compensatory leave days in place of overtime pay. The MHRSD awareness guide says such leave must be at least 1.5 hours per overtime hour, used within 60 days unless agreed otherwise, and capped at 30 days a year. Annual cap: 720 overtime hours a year, which may be exceeded with the worker's consent (ministerial decision; MHRSD Knowledge Centre).
overtime.summary_ar: المادة 107 (معدلة): يدفع صاحب العمل للعامل عن ساعات العمل الإضافية أجراً إضافياً يوازي أجر الساعة (الفعلي) مضافاً إليه 50% من أجره الأساسي، ويجوز بموافقة العامل احتساب أيام إجازة مدفوعة الأجر عوضاً عن أجر الساعات الإضافية. لا تزيد ساعات العمل الإضافية على 720 ساعة في السنة إلا بموافقة العامل.

overtime.notes: The rate formula and the compensatory-leave option are confirmed from MHRSD excerpts. The 720 h cap is on an older Knowledge Centre page tied to a ministerial decision, and the law delegates the cap to the Minister. I could not confirm that it still stands after 2025, so treat the cap as secondary. The 1.5h / 60-day / 30-day compensatory-leave details come only from the awareness-guide excerpt. Some vendor calculators wrongly use basic*1.5; the MHRSD method uses actual + 0.5*basic. The /30/8 divisor comes from the MHRSD example, not statute text. working_hours.summary_en: Article 98. Actual working hours may not exceed 8 hours a day if the employer uses a daily standard, or 48 hours a week if it uses a weekly standard. During Ramadan, hours for Muslim workers are reduced to at most 6 a day or 36 a week. Overtime hours are additional and paid under Article 107.
working_hours.summary_ar: المادة 98: لا يجوز تشغيل العامل تشغيلاً فعلياً أكثر من ثماني ساعات في اليوم إذا اعتمد المعيار اليومي، أو أكثر من ثمانٍ وأربعين ساعة في الأسبوع إذا اعتمد المعيار الأسبوعي، وتخفض ساعات العمل الفعلية خلال شهر رمضان للعمال المسلمين بحيث لا تزيد على ست ساعات في اليوم أو ست وثلاثين ساعة في الأسبوع.

working_hours.notes: The values match long-standing Article 98 text and annual MHRSD Ramadan announcements reported by press. The MHRSD Knowledge Centre page was found but its text was not read, so these values are secondary rather than confirmed. Commentators dispute whether the Ramadan reduction applies to non-Muslims; the text says Muslim workers. I found no report that M/44 changed Article 98.

annual_leave.summary_en: Article 109. Paid annual leave of at least 21 days a year, rising to at least 30 days once the worker completes 5 consecutive years with the same employer. The leave wage is paid IN ADVANCE, before the leave starts. Leave should be taken in the year it falls due. The worker may not waive it or take cash instead during employment. It may be postponed or split with employer approval.
annual_leave.summary_ar: المادة 109: يستحق العامل عن كل عام إجازة سنوية لا تقل مدتها عن واحد وعشرين يوماً، تزاد إلى مدة لا تقل عن ثلاثين يوماً إذا أمضى العامل في خدمة صاحب العمل خمس سنوات متصلة، بأجر يدفع مقدماً. ولا يجوز للعامل التنازل عنها أو تقاضي بدل نقدي عنها أثناء الخدمة.

leave_compensation.summary_en: Article 111. A worker who leaves before using accrued annual leave is entitled to the wage for those unused days. The worker is also entitled to leave wage for the fraction of the year worked, in proportion to the time worked. The payment is made at the worker's wage; the prevailing reading is the actual wage.
leave_compensation.summary_ar: المادة 111: للعامل الحق في الحصول على أجر عن أيام الإجازة المستحقة إذا ترك العمل قبل استعماله لها، وذلك بالنسبة إلى المدة التي لم يحصل على إجازته عنها، كما يستحق أجر الإجازة عن أجزاء السنة بنسبة ما قضاه منها في العمل.

notice_period.summary_en: Article 75, as amended and in force from 19 Feb 2025, applies to INDEFINITE contracts terminated for a legitimate reason. If the worker's wage is paid monthly, a worker who terminates must give at least 30 days' written notice, and an employer who terminates must give at least 60 days. If the wage is not paid monthly, either party must give at least 30 days. Under the pre-2025 rule, each party gave at least 60 days (monthly paid) or 30 days (others), with no split by who terminates. Article 76: a party who does not observe the notice period must pay the other the worker's wage for the notice period, unless agreed otherwise. A worker given notice by the employer may be absent one full day a week, or 8 hours during the week, with pay, to look for work. Article 77 (termination for an illegitimate reason, absent an agreed amount) gives compensation of 15 days' wage per year of service for an indefinite contract, or the wage for the remaining term for a fixed-term contract, with a minimum of 2 months' wage in either case.
notice_period.summary_ar: المادة 75 (معدلة): إذا كان العقد غير محدد المدة جاز لأي من طرفيه إنهاؤه بناءً على سبب مشروع بإشعار كتابي للطرف الآخر قبل الإنهاء بمدة لا تقل عن ثلاثين يوماً إذا كان الإنهاء من العامل، ولا تقل عن ستين يوماً إذا كان من صاحب العمل، متى كان أجر العامل يدفع شهرياً، ولا تقل عن ثلاثين يوماً لغيره. المادة 76: إذا لم يراعِ الطرف المنهي مدة الإشعار التزم بأن يدفع للطرف الآخر مبلغاً مساوياً لأجر العامل عن مدة الإشعار ما لم يتفق الطرفان على خلافه. المادة 77: التعويض عن الإنهاء لسبب غير مشروع أجر 15 يوماً عن كل سنة (غير محدد المدة) أو أجر المدة الباقية (محدد المدة) بحد أدنى أجر شهرين.

fixed_term_contracts.summary_en: Article 37, as amended in 2025: a non-Saudi worker's contract must be written and fixed-term. If no term is stated, the contract is deemed to run for ONE YEAR from the worker's actual start date. If both parties continue performing it, it is deemed renewed for a similar period. Before 19 Feb 2025, the default term was the work permit's duration. Article 55: a fixed-term contract ends when its term expires, and if both parties continue performing it, it is deemed renewed for an indefinite period, subject to Article 37 for non-Saudis. For Saudis, MHRSD guidance says a fixed-term contract converts to indefinite after 3 consecutive renewals, or when the original term plus renewals reaches 4 years, whichever is less.
fixed_term_contracts.summary_ar: المادة 37 (معدلة): يجب أن يكون عقد عمل غير السعودي مكتوباً ومحدد المدة، وإذا خلا العقد من بيان مدته عُدَّ لمدة سنة من تاريخ مباشرة العامل للعمل، وإذا استمر طرفاه في تنفيذه عُدَّ العقد مجدداً لمدة مماثلة. المادة 55: ينتهي العقد المحدد المدة بانقضاء مدته، فإذا استمر الطرفان في تنفيذه عُدَّ مجدداً لمدة غير محددة مع مراعاة المادة 37 لغير السعوديين، ويتحول عقد السعودي إلى غير محدد المدة إذا تجدد ثلاث مرات متتالية أو بلغت مدته الأصلية مع مدة التجديد أربع سنوات أيهما أقل.

gosi_saudi_legacy.summary_en: Applies to Saudi private-sector employees who had contribution periods before the new Social Insurance Law took effect on 3 Jul 2024. They stay on the old Social Insurance Law. The annuities branch is 18% of the contributory wage, split 9% employee and 9% employer. SANED unemployment insurance is 1.5%, split 0.75% each, a rate in force since 1 Jan 2022 after a cut from 2%. Occupational hazards is 2%, paid by the employer only. The totals are 9.75% employee, 11.75% employer, 21.5% overall. Under the old law, no rate increase applies in 2025 or 2026.
gosi_saudi_legacy.summary_ar: للمشتركين السعوديين القائمين (ممن لهم مدد اشتراك قبل 3 يوليو 2024): فرع المعاشات 18% (9% على المشترك و9% على صاحب العمل)، والتعطل عن العمل (ساند) 1.5% مناصفة (0.75% لكل طرف) منذ 1/1/2022، والأخطار المهنية 2% على صاحب العمل؛ الإجمالي 9.75% على الموظف و11.75% على صاحب العمل.

gosi_saudi_new_law.summary_en: The new Social Insurance Law (Royal Decree M/273) took effect on 3 Jul 2024 (27/12/1445H). It applies ONLY to people who join the labour market with NO prior contribution period under either the Civil Retirement Law or the Social Insurance Law before that date; existing contributors stay on the old law. The annuities rate starts at 9% each for employee and employer. From the 2nd year of the law through the 5th, it rises 0.5 percentage points each on every 1 July, reaching 11% each by 1 Jul 2028. SANED (0.75% each) and occupational hazards (2%, employer) are unchanged. The rates in force on 2026-11-03 (from 1 Jul 2026) are annuities 10% each, so the employee pays 10.75%, the employer 12.75%, and the total is 23.5%. The law also sets the statutory retirement age at 65.
gosi_saudi_new_law.summary_ar: نظام التأمينات الاجتماعية الجديد (المرسوم الملكي م/273) ساري من 3 يوليو 2024 على الملتحقين بسوق العمل ممن ليس لهم مدد اشتراك سابقة في نظامي التقاعد المدني أو التأمينات الاجتماعية. نسبة فرع المعاشات تبدأ 9% لكل من المشترك وصاحب العمل وتزداد 0.5% في 1 يوليو من كل عام حتى تبلغ 11% في يوليو 2028. النسبة الحالية (من 1 يوليو 2026): 10% لكل طرف، فيصبح إجمالي استقطاع الموظف 10.75% وصاحب العمل 12.75%.

gosi_wage_limits.summary_en: The contributory wage is the basic wage plus housing allowance, whether housing is paid in cash or provided in kind. salary_payment.summary_en: Private sector (Article 90): wages are paid in the official currency. A worker on a monthly wage must be paid at least once a month, and other pay frequencies have their own minimums. Salaries are paid through the Wage Protection System via MHRSD's Mudad platform, where employers upload wage files. Press reports MHRSD inspection triggers when wage files are more than 20 days late, and a vendor reports a 30-day upload cutoff from 1 Mar 2025. The Labor Law sets NO fixed calendar payday for the private sector. Government sector: Ministry of Finance pays civil and military state salaries on the 27th of each Gregorian month. If the 27th is a Friday, payment moves to the Thursday before, and if it is a Saturday, to the Sunday after. This follows Cabinet Decision No. 551 of 25/12/1437H, under Royal Decree M/6 of 12/4/1407H.
salary_payment.summary_ar: القطاع الخاص (المادة 90): تُدفع الأجور بالعملة الرسمية، ويُدفع أجر العامل الشهري مرة في الشهر على الأقل، وتُصرف عبر نظام حماية الأجور (منصة مدد) دون يوم محدد نظاماً. القطاع الحكومي: تصرف وزارة المالية رواتب موظفي الدولة يوم 27 من كل شهر ميلادي، فإن وافق الجمعة فالخميس الذي قبله، وإن وافق السبت فالأحد الذي بعده (قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم 551 وتاريخ 25/12/1437هـ).

vat.summary_en: Standard VAT in Saudi Arabia is 15%, effective 1 July 2020 (up from 5%). It applies to electricity and water/wastewater bills (consumption and fixed or meter charges; published electricity tariffs exclude VAT), fuel at the pump (believed VAT-inclusive), Fahas inspection (SAR 100 + 15% = 115) and commercial EV charging. Government fees charged as a public authority, such as istimara, driving licences, plates and ownership transfer, are outside the VAT scope.

university_weighted_admission.summary_en: Saudi universities rank applicants by a weighted percentage (النسبة الموزونة) combining high-school GPA (%), Qudurat (General Aptitude Test, out of 100) and Tahsili (Achievement Test, out of 100), all from Qiyas/ETEC. Most common split for science/health tracks: 30% high school + 30% Qudurat + 40% Tahsili. Weights vary by university, track and program and are published before each cycle; there is no fixed cutoff—admission depends on ranking and seats. Confirmed examples: IAU 30/30/40 (official admission calculator); KSU health programs (e.g., Midwifery) 30/30/40, Medicine 30/30/40 plus interview; KFUPM regular track 10% high school + 50% Qudurat + 40% Tahsili, KFUPM primary/early track 50% Qudurat + 50% KFUPM achievement test; KAU uses track-specific tables (1447 guide shows 30/30/40 components; preparatory-year variants such as 40/40/20 in older guides).

government_payday.summary_en: Government employees' salaries are paid on the 27th of each Gregorian month, per Royal directive / Cabinet decision effective from the 2016–2017 fiscal year (first Gregorian payday 27 Oct 2016 per Ministry of Finance).
